input.quote: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
input.rationale: § 7.6 imposes liquidated damages payable by Customer (USD 25,000 per day) triggered by "any delay in providing a dependency" — a minor, uncapped trigger with no notice, materiality threshold, or aggregate cap. This fails both the preferred position (no Customer-payable liquidated damages or penalties) and the fallback (a single early-termination fee capped at three months' fees), and the uncapped daily accrual for minor breaches approaches walk-away territory. No other Customer-payable liquidated damages, penalty, or minimum termination fee appears in the document, and there is no offsetting service-credit regime in the body of the agreement. Redline deletes the liquidated damages and substitutes a good-faith equitable adjustment of the affected schedule, which preserves Vendor's legitimate relief for delays it did not cause.

proposal.summary: Delete Customer-payable USD 25,000/day liquidated damages for dependency delay; replace with equitable timeline adjustment
proposal.comment: [Playbook] We cannot accept liquidated damages or penalties payable by us, and an uncapped USD 25,000 per day charge for any dependency delay is punitive relative to the harm. We have replaced it with a good-faith equitable adjustment of the affected schedule, with Vendor's actual reasonable costs remaining recoverable.

ops.oldText: 7.6 Customer shall pay Vendor USD 25,000 per day as agreed liquidated damages for any delay in providing a dependency.
ops.newText: 7.6 If Customer does not provide a dependency on time and that delay actually affects Vendor's performance, Vendor shall promptly notify Customer and the Parties will agree in good faith an equitable adjustment to the affected schedule or deliverable dates. Customer shall not be liable for any liquidated damages, penalty, or similar pre-agreed sum in respect of such delay.
